<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions

col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

</asp>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Row and column indices (0‑based)
row(R) :- n_rows(N), R >= 0, R < N.
col(C) :- n_cols(M), C >= 0, C < M.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Helper predicate – each output cell must get exactly one colour
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

1 { output(R,C,Colour) : colour(C) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Find the vertical line of 3‑2‑3 (2 in the middle, 3 above and below)
%   has2(P,Q) is true iff column Q contains 2 with a 3 directly above
%   and a 3 directly below it.
has2(P,Q) :- input(P,Q,2),
             input(P-1,Q,3),
             input(P+1,Q,3),
             row(P), col(Q), P >= 1, P <= N-2.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% The three rows that belong to the vertical line:
%   • the row above the 2   (P‑1)
%   • the row containing the 2 (P)
%   • the row below the 2   (P+1)
% For each of these rows we will fill the cells that are to the
%   left of the pivot column Q (i.e. all columns C with C ≤ Q).
%   The colour used is the colour that already appears at column Q in
%   that particular row (3, 2 or 3).
special(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = P-1, row(R), col(C), C >= 0, C <= Q.
special(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = P,   row(R), col(C), C >= 0, C <= Q.
special(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = P+1, row(R), col(C), C >= 0, C <= Q.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Output for the three “special’’ rows – inherit the colour from column Q
output(R,C,Colour) :- special(R,C), Colour = input(R,Q).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% For all other cells copy the input unchanged
output(R,C,Colour) :- row(R), col(C), input(R,C,Colour), not special(R,C).

#show output/3.

            input(P0-1,Q,3), input(P0+1,Q,3).

% All other cells copy the input unchanged
output(R,C,Color) :- not special_cell(R,C), input(R,C,Color).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Helper predicates for cell positions
row(R) :- n_rows(N), R = 0..N-1.
col(C) :- n_cols(M), C = 0..M-1.

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour for each output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Pivot detection: a 2 with a 3 directly above and below it in the same column
has2(P,Q) :- input(P,Q,2), P = P0, P0 >= 1, P0+1 < N,
            input(P0-1,Q,3), input(P0+1,Q,3).

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
% Special cells – left side of the rows around the pivot
special_cell(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = R1, R1 = P-1, C = C1, C1 >= 0, C1 <= R1-1.
special_cell(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = P,   C = C2, C2 >= 0, C2 <= R-1.
special_cell(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = P+1, C = C3, C3 >= 0, C3 <= (P+1)-1.

% Special cells inherit the colour from column Q of the same row
output(R,C,Color) :- special_cell(R,C), Color = input(R,Q).

% All other cells copy the input unchanged
output(R,C,Color) :- not special_cell(R,C), input(R,C,Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- #count{R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.

% Row and column indices
row(R) :- n_rows(N), R >= 0, R < N.
col(C) :- n_cols(M), C >= 0, C < M.

% Output cell predicate
output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Exactly one colour for each output cell
1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Col) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Find the 2 with a 3 above and below in the same column (vertical line)
has2(P,Q) :- input(P,Q,2), input(P-1,Q,3), input(P+1,Q,3),
            row(P), col(Q), P >= 1, P <= N-2.

% Special rows: the three rows containing the pivot line
special(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = P-1, row(R), col(C), C >= 0, C <= Q.
special(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = P,   row(R), col(C), C >= 0, C <= Q.
special(R,C) :- has2(P,Q), R = P+1, row(R), col(C), C >= 0, C <= Q.

% Output for the three special rows: inherit the colour from column Q of that row
output(R,C,Color) :- special(R,C), Color = input(R,Q).

% Output for all other cells: copy the input
output(R,C,Color) :- row(R), col(C), input(R,C,Color), not special(R,C).

n_cols(M) :- #count{C : input(_, C, _) }.

has2(P,Q) :- input(P,Q,2),

             input(P+1,Q,3),

% -----------------------------------------------------------------

% -----------------------------------------------------------------
